result.summary: Adds a TxCollection interface to the mining IPC and node subsystems, enabling external callers to reconstruct and validate block templates from an ordered list of witness transaction IDs. Matches requested transactions against the local node's mempool, provides an API to identify and submit missing transactions, and validates the assembled candidate block with TestBlockValidity. Reusable coinbase creation logic is extracted from BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock() into a helper, while mempool-specific methods on externally assembled templates are disabled.
result.problem: External mining servers approving miner-selected templates (such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers) currently must maintain an independent mirror mempool by repeatedly querying block templates and polling for missing transactions. This duplicates mempool accounting outside the Bitcoin Core node and wastes memory and IPC bandwidth.
evidence: PR description: 'The new TxCollection interface introduced by this PR removes the need for such a mirror mempool. We build the block template ourselves now, based on the requested transaction list and our own mempool.'
PR description notes end-to-end demonstration in Stratum v2 Reference Implementation: 'The following flow is demonstrated in https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-apps/pull/599'
result.scope_notes: Extracts BlockAssembler::CreateCoinbaseTx() from BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock() as a non-behavior-changing refactor to share coinbase construction between internal template generation and TxCollection dummy-coinbase validation.
result.card: Adds a TxCollection mining IPC interface allowing external services like Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS) to assemble and validate candidate block templates from a list of witness transaction IDs using the local node's mempool. External template validators currently have to maintain a separate out-of-process mirror mempool and poll full templates or missing transactions, duplicating state and wasting bandwidth. The new interface identifies which transactions are missing, ingests them from the client, and validates the resulting block template against the chain tip using TestBlockValidity. Demonstrated against the Stratum v2 reference implementation in sv2-apps PR 599.
